## Admin Division
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/admin-division-1389896348-2025-02-26

Admin Division
Admin Division
×
Print
Admin Division
Functions:
The Admin Division at PTA is responsible for managing administrative operations, procurement functions and overseeing civil projects. It ensures the smooth functioning of office facilities, including maintenance of buildings, utilities, and security arrangements. The division handles procurement, vendor management, and contracts related to office supplies and civil works. It also oversees construction, renovation, and maintenance projects to ensure compliance with regulatory standards. Additionally, it manages official transport, logistics, and event coordination while ensuring workplace safety and security. Through effective administration and infrastructure management, the division plays a vital role in supporting PTA’s operational efficiency.

## Muzaffarabad
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/muzaffarabad-841795321-2023-05-30

Muzaffarabad
Muzaffarabad
×
Print
Muzaffarabad
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Muzaffarabad provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
Director Enforcement, PTA Zonal office, B-92, Upper Chatter Housing Scheme, Muzaffarabad.
For Complaints:
Phone
Fax
Email
Address

+92-5822-921199

## Faisalabad
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/faisalabad-167391310-2023-05-30

Faisalabad
Faisalabad
×
Print
Faisalabad
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Faisalabad provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
House No. 11-Y-103, Main Double Road, Susan Road, Madina Town, Faisalabad.
For Complaints:

## Wireline Licensing
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/licensing-721279833-2023-05-30

Wireline Licensing
Wireline Licensing
×
Print
Wireline Licensing
Functions:
The Wireline Licensing Division consists of two directorates, i.e Wireline Licensing and Numbering. The Wireline Directorate is responsible for administering the licensing for Pakistan's fixed-line Telecommunications sector. It oversees the licensing of LDI, FLL, TIP, TTP, TPSP, Data/VPN/VTS and District-Level Internet Services, as well as the registration of SMS Aggregator and Content Services, in accordance with the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) Act, 1996, and the applicable regulatory framework.
The Numbering Directorate is responsible for allocation and administration of numbering resources, i.e Geographic Numbers, Toll Free Numbers, UAN, Short Codes, etc.
The Wireline Licensing Division facilitates market entry, promotes regulatory compliance, and supports the orderly growth of telecommunications networks, infrastructure, and services across the country.

## Functions
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/functions-1487939166-2023-05-30

Functions
Functions
×
Print
Functions
PTA's functions include:
To regulate the establishment, operation and maintenance of telecommunication systems and provision of telecommunication services in Pakistan.
To receive and expeditiously dispose of applications for the use of radio-frequency spectrum.
To promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services in Pakistan.
To promote the availability of a wide range of high quality, efficient, cost effective and competitive telecommunication services throughout Pakistan.
To promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
To investigate and adjudicate on complaints and other claims made against licensees arising out of alleged contraventions of the provisions of this Act, the rules made and licenses issued there under and take action accordingly.
To make recommendations to the Federal Government on policies with respect to international telecommunications, provision of support for participation in international meetings and agreements to be executed in relation to the routing of international traffic and accounting settlements.
To perform such other functions as the Federal Government may assign from time to time.

## Audit
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/audit-679526975-2025-09-16

Audit
Audit
×
Print
Audit
Functions:
The Audit Division of Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) plays a critical role in ensuring transparency, accountability, and compliance within the organization. It conducts financial, operational, and performance audits to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls and the efficient utilization of resources. The division reviews financial transactions, regulatory receipts, and expenditures in line with government rules and PTA’s service regulations. It also provides recommendations to strengthen governance, minimize risks, and prevent irregularities. By maintaining oversight and ensuring adherence to regulatory and financial standards, the Audit Division supports PTA’s mission of good governance and institutional integrity.

## International | NT CERT
- **Source URL**: https://ntcert.pta.gov.pk/international.html

International | NT CERT
National Collaboration
Home
National Collaboration
International Collaboration
In the rapidly evolving landscape of cybersecurity, international collaboration is paramount to effectively address and mitigate cyber threats. ntCERT is a part of a global network of Computer Emergency Response Teams (CERTs) that work together to enhance cybersecurity resilience and response capabilities. Below are some of our esteemed international partners:
Asia Pacific Computer Emergency Response Team (APCERT), https://www.apcert.org/
Bhutan Computer Incident Response Team (BtCIRT), https://www.btcirt.bt/
Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (SLCERT), https://cert.gov.lk/
Malaysia Computer Emergency Response Team (MyCERT), https://www.mycert.org.my/
NT CERT
National Telecom CERT
Pak Telecom CERT
Pak CERT
Pakistan CERT
Cyber Security Pakistan

## WeProtect Global Summit 2024
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/weprotect-global-summit-2024-1190197799-2025-02-18

WeProtect Global Summit 2024
WeProtect Global Summit 2024
×
Print
WeProtect Global Summit 2024
WeProtect Global Alliance in collaboration with Ministry of Interior UAE invited PTA officers to attend the WeProtect Global Summit 2024 in Abu Dhabi, a gathering of policymakers, experts and stakeholders dedicated to combat online child exploitation. The summit featured insightful sessions by specialists, offering valuable perspectives on complex issues and emerging threats surrounding child online protection. A significant highlight of the event was the opportunity to listen to the courageous stories of survivors and children who have faced hardships throughout their journey. The summit underscored the transformative power of collective action on a global scale, emphasizing the importance of collaboration and cooperation to effectively address the pressing issue of child online protection.

## Gwadar
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/gwadar-1223229190-2023-05-30

Gwadar
Gwadar
×
Print
Gwadar
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Gwadar provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
House No. BH-3, Phase-I, New Town, Gwadar.

## Gilgit Baltistan
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/gilgit-baltistan-454270396-2023-05-30

Gilgit Baltistan
Gilgit Baltistan
×
Print
Gilgit Baltistan
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Gilgat Baltistan provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
Director Enforcement
PTA Zonal Office Gilgit,
Near Rupal Inn, Shahrah-e-Quaid-e-Azam, Khomer, Jutial Cantt, Gilgit.

Chairman's Message
At the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), we are committed to building a digitally inclusive, secure, and forward-looking Pakistan. Our mission is to ensure that every citizen regardless of geography or background, has access to reliable, affordable, and high-quality telecommunications and digital services.
In today’s fast evolving world, digital connectivity is no longer a luxury, it is a fundamental enabler for education, healthcare, business, and social inclusion. On this transformative journey, PTA stands as both a catalyst and a guardian of progress, shaping regulatory and licensing landscape guided by technological advancement that not only support innovation but also protect the rights and interests of users.
In line with this commitment, we take pride in remarkable strides made by Pakistan’s telecom sector including record growth in telecom subscribers, substantial expansion of  broadband coverage and the local manufacturing of millions of mobile devices. PTA has also laid the foundation for adoption of future technologies such as 5G, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and advanced Wi-Fi standards, ensuring that Pakistan remains at the forefront of digital transformation. These achievements are not merely milestones for the industry but represent steps toward creating a technologically advanced Pakistan and strengthening the national economy.
Yet, our work is far from done. We are steadfast in our resolve to bridge the digital divide, enhance cybersecurity, encourage public private collaboration, and ensure that Pakistan is ready to embrace the future technological advancements. As we move forward, transparency, consumer protection, and equitable growth will remain at the heart of all our initiatives.
On behalf of PTA, I extend my sincere gratitude to the telecom industry, partners, and the people of Pakistan for their trust and support. Together, we will continue to shape a resilient digital future, one that ensures connectivity, opportunity, safety, and prosperity for the people of Pakistan.

## HR & Coord
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/hr-&-coord-140628289-2025-02-26

HR & Coord
HR & Coord
×
Print
HR & Coord
Functions:
The Human Resource & Coordination (HR & Coord) Division at PTA is responsible for managing personnel affairs, organizational development, and to ensure strong administrative coordination across various units of the organization. It oversees recruitment, performance evaluation, career progression and employee benefits while ensuring compliance with PTA regulations. The division formulates and implements HR policies, organizes training programs for employee development and addresses workplace concerns, grievances and disciplinary matters. Additionally, the division serves as a key liaison between internal departments, external organizations, and government entities, facilitating smooth communication and coordination. Maintaining employee records and ensuring compliance with labor laws and organizational policies are also integral functions of this division, contributing to an efficient and well-structured workforce within PTA. Additionally, the division is responsible for overseeing health facilities and developing policies to enhance employee and its family’s welfare. It also coordinates with hospitals to ensure employees receive the best possible treatment in medical situations.

## Long Distance & International
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/long-distance-international-1338039894-2023-05-30

Long Distance & International
Long Distance & International
×
Print
Long Distance & International
Pakistan Telecommunication Authority is not receiving applications for Long Distance and International (LD&I) licenses for Pakistan, Azad Jammu & Kashmir (AJ&K), and Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) till further notice.
Long Distance and International (LDI) license is issued for the provision of end-to-end communication between points that are located in Pakistan with points that are located outside of Pakistan.
Information Memorandum
FAQs - LDI
Application Processing
Document Required for Creating Organization Profile in OASIS
Information to be provided by Applicant
As part of the Application, an Applicant must provide the following via “Online Application Submission Information System (OASIS).”
Letter of Application
Checklist
Fees in the following amounts is payable in Pak Rupees:
Application fee of US $ 500 (or equivalent Forex value in PKR)
Initial fee – LDI License of US $ 500,000/- (or equivalent Forex value in PKR) (after approval of the Authority for Grant of License)
A Performance Bank Guarantee of US $ 10 Million (or equivalent Forex value in PKR) in favour of the Authority.
Certificate of Incorporation of the Applicant and its Memorandum and Articles of Association;
Names of the Directors of the Applicant, and relation of each Director to any other Operator licensed by the Authority or any other Applicant for a License;
Shareholders of the Applicant, including details of each shareholder’s equity ownership;
Names of each Affiliate of a shareholder of the Applicant, where the Affiliate is an Operator or an applicant for a License, and description of the relation to the Applicant;
Copies of National Identity Card (for Pakistani nationals) / Passport (foreign nationals) and other antecedents of the Directors and authorized representative of the company.
Provide an undertaking for the following:
That the Company or its Directors have never been declared insolvent by a court of law
That the Directors of the company have never been convicted by a court of law for major offences or unethical/immoral turpitude (other than minor offences)
That neither the applicant Company nor its group/consortium members are defaulter (s) with reference to other PTA licenses/transactions.
Applicant’s National Income tax number;
Certificate on original letterhead from the Group/Joint venture/Consortium members that they are the participants for LDI license in Pakistan through the applicant company.
Certificate of good standing with the fiscal administration;
Resolution of the Board of Directors of the Applicant authorizing the individual who submits and signs the Application.
Special Power of Attorney by the Applicant authorizing the individual who submits and signs the Application.
A brief description of the following:
Telecommunication experience of the Applicant, its key management personnel and its shareholders.
Business plan for the initial five years of operations, indicating areas to be served, services to be offered, projected revenues, operating expenses and capital requirements.
Committed financial resources including a list of all sources and amounts of equity and debt financing required to finance the business plan in the first 5 years of operation. Capital must show at least a 20% equity component.
Technical plan, including proposed network map and architecture.
Affidavit of the person granted the power of attorney by the Applicant.
The Applicant shall submit the application on “Online Application Submission Information System (OASIS).”
Upon receipt, the Authority will provide an acknowledgement of the received Application via “Online Application Submission Information System (OASIS).”
Eligibility Criteria
The following are the eligibility requirements for a License:
The applicant shall be an incorporated or registered company in Pakistan under the Companies Ordinance, 1984.
The applicant submits all the documents mentioned above.

## ICT Division
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/ict-division-637266382-2025-02-26

ICT Division
ICT Division
×
Print
ICT Division
Functions:
The ICT Division of PTA is responsible for managing and overseeing the organization's information and communication technology infrastructure. Its role includes ensuring the seamless operation of IT systems, network security, data management, and digital services. The division plays a critical role in implementing and maintaining technology-driven solutions to support regulatory functions, enhance operational efficiency, and ensure cybersecurity compliance. It is also responsible for the development and deployment of digital platforms, automation of processes, and integration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and cloud computing. Additionally, the ICT Division provides technical support, manages enterprise software, and ensures the reliability and security of communication networks within PTA.

Chairman's Message
At the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), we are committed to building a digitally inclusive, secure, and forward-looking Pakistan. Our mission is to ensure that every citizen regardless of geography or background, has access to reliable, affordable, and high-quality telecommunications and digital services.
In today’s fast evolving world, digital connectivity is no longer a luxury, it is a fundamental enabler for education, healthcare, business, and social inclusion. On this transformative journey, PTA stands as both a catalyst and a guardian of progress, shaping regulatory and licensing landscape guided by technological advancement that not only support innovation but also protect the rights and interests of users.
In line with this commitment, we take pride in remarkable strides made by Pakistan’s telecom sector including record growth in telecom subscribers, substantial expansion of  broadband coverage and the local manufacturing of millions of mobile devices. PTA has also laid the foundation for adoption of future technologies such as 5G, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and advanced Wi-Fi standards, ensuring that Pakistan remains at the forefront of digital transformation. These achievements are not merely milestones for the industry but represent steps toward creating a technologically advanced Pakistan and strengthening the national economy.
Yet, our work is far from done. We are steadfast in our resolve to bridge the digital divide, enhance cybersecurity, encourage public private collaboration, and ensure that Pakistan is ready to embrace the future technological advancements. As we move forward, transparency, consumer protection, and equitable growth will remain at the heart of all our initiatives.
On behalf of PTA, I extend my sincere gratitude to the telecom industry, partners, and the people of Pakistan for their trust and support. Together, we will continue to shape a resilient digital future, one that ensures connectivity, opportunity, safety, and prosperity for the people of Pakistan.

## Strategy & Development
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/strategy-&-development-795113932-2025-02-26

Strategy & Development
Strategy & Development
×
Print
Strategy & Development
Functions:
Strategy and Development (S&D) division, being an important organ of PTA, is responsible for performing functions summarized as below: Explore and analyze emerging/current technologies, latest regulatory trends in telecom industry. Assist Authority by providing input on technical, strategic and policy matters related to regulation of Telecommunication sector. Development of regulatory frameworks/instruments in pace with technology evolution and telecom services uptake/adoption Conducting workshops and capacity building initiatives with vendors and telecom industry stakeholders. Liaison/coordination with internal and external stakeholders on policy and regulatory affairs.

## SAMENA LEAD Award 2024
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/samena-lead-award-2024-372109257-2025-02-18

SAMENA LEAD Award 2024
SAMENA LEAD Award 2024
×
Print
SAMENA LEAD Award 2024
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has again won the prestigious LEAD Award in the “Regulatory Enablement” category by the SAMENA Telecommunications Council 2024.
This is the second consecutive year that the PTA has received this award, recognizing its dedication to ensuring digital safety for children across Pakistan.
PTA’s leadership in child online protection has been pivotal in creating a safer digital environment. Collaborating with international organizations like GSMA and UNICEF, ITU’s Council Working Group on Child Online Protection, PTA has played a key global role in advancing online safety.
In 2023 and 2024, PTA launched a nationwide Training of Trainers (ToT) program, training 15 master trainers who are now educating 210 facilitators. These facilitators will, in turn, teach children, parents, and teachers about digital safety, expanding the program’s reach across communities.

## Enforcement
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/enforcement-1668605255-2023-05-30

Enforcement
Enforcement
×
Print
Enforcement
Functions:
The Enforcement Division of PTA is responsible for ensuring compliance with regulatory frameworks, policies, and directives issued by the Authority. It monitors telecom operators and service providers to verify adherence to licensing conditions, quality of service standards, and consumer protection regulations. The division investigates violations, takes enforcement actions against non-compliance, and imposes penalties where necessary. It also collaborates with legal and technical departments to address regulatory breaches and works towards ensuring a fair and transparent telecom environment. Additionally, the division plays a key role in handling complaints, conducting inspections, and coordinating with stakeholders to uphold the integrity of the telecommunications sector.

## Speed Test App
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/speed-test-app-705263700-2023-05-30

Speed Test App
Speed Test App
×
Print
Speed Test App
PTA speed test application helps users check their internet speed and experience (internet speed) they may have with their operators. It can also give user’s quick confirmation of the max speed they can achieve from their respective operators. Users can use this app to ensure if they are connected to the internet. The application logs the network preference mode and the operator of the user which can educate the users to understand and differentiate among other operators. Having any speed related issue, users can give their feedback which will help the operators to understand their governed issues. The Lat/Long logged can assist to identify the strong and weak spots for the operators and developers.
Download PTA Speed Test App
Features:
Users can stop the ongoing test.
Speed test details are stored in database and can be viewed later in Log tab.
Test history can be saved in phone storage in csv format.
User can delete all the previously conducted test's history
How it works:
It checks availability of location service and internet connection. In case services are disabled, app prompts user to enable services for accurate results.
It also check network connection type i.e. either 3g, 4g, LTE or Wi-Fi internet.
Depending upon the type of internet connection and the estimated maximum speed it can provide, app decides the size of file to be uploaded or downloaded to/from the server.
Separate threads for ping, upload and download are executed.
Thread Start and end time is properly calculated.
Within the time frame app send and receive data to/from server and calculate the speed (bytes per second).
After the thread complete its calculation, final values for ping, upload and download are displayed to the user and saved in log for future use.
-- Ping:
Measuring the time it takes to get a response for a http request sent to the server.
It is repeated twice with the lowest value determining the final result.
-- Download:
Based on the internet connection type, one of multiple file sizes is selected to download from server.
Data packets are received and calculated as bytes per second.
-- Upload:
Based on the internet connection type, file size is decided for upload to server.
Data bytes are pushed to the server via POST request.
Packets are sorted by speed, and the fastest half is used to determine the result.

## Rawalpindi
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/rawalpindi-463272203-2023-05-30

Rawalpindi
Rawalpindi
×
Print
Rawalpindi
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Rawalpindi provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
Director (Enforcement) PTA Zonal Office, Adjacent to PTCL Cantt Exchange, Kashmir Road, Rawalpindi.
For Complaints:
Phone
Fax
Email
Address
+92-51-5766402
+92-51-5766403
rawalpindi@pta.gov.pk
PTA Zonal Office, Adjacent to PTCL Cantt Exchange The Mall Rawalpindi Cantt

## Introduction
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/introduction-55493323-2025-02-18

Introduction
Introduction
×
Print
Introduction
For the guidance of our young audience and their parents, PTA has curated valuable resources covering various topics on Child Online Protection. This material is designed to educate children, parents, caregivers and teachers on prevailing online risks & its preventive technical plus wellbeing measures, ensuring a secure online environment for children. Our aim is to provide guidance to children, parents, caregivers and teachers in local language and ensuring easy access to awareness content and tools that can help navigate the digital world safely. Explore our selection and find resources tailored to your needs.

## Collaboration with TikTok
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/collaboration-with-tiktok-306375254-2025-02-18

Collaboration with TikTok
Collaboration with TikTok
×
Print
Collaboration with TikTok
MoU between PTA and TikTok was signed for making Internet Safe and Secure for Young People.  As per MoU, training is being imparted to parents, teacher and students in 100 Gov’t schools in 1st phase. So far training has been completed in Sindh and Gilgit. For training, study material including Children’s Toolkit, Digital Hifazat Workbook, Comic Book for students and Parents Guideline was developed and uploaded over PTA’s website for public. Additionally, 5x short awareness videos covering various important online safety topics necessary for students were developed and disseminated through Social Media.

## Wireless Licensing
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/wireless-licensing-696143813-2025-02-26

Wireless Licensing
Wireless Licensing
×
Print
Wireless Licensing
Functions:
The Wireless Licensing Division of PTA is responsible for managing the licensing process for wireless communication services in Pakistan. Its role includes evaluating applications, issuing licenses, and ensuring compliance with regulatory frameworks for wireless spectrum usage. The division works to facilitate the efficient allocation of frequency spectrum, prevent interference, and promote fair competition in the telecommunications sector. It also coordinates with relevant stakeholders, including government bodies and service providers, to ensure adherence to national and international standards. It is also responsible for the identification / mitigation of Grey traffic, web filtering actions under PECA 2016 and Internet Governance initiatives such as Internet Exchange Points (IXP), IP Whitelisting and VPN registration. Additionally, the division plays a key role in policy development, spectrum pricing, and monitoring the utilization of licensed frequencies to optimize wireless communication infrastructure.

## Peshawar
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/peshawar-503968114-2023-05-30

Peshawar
Peshawar
×
Print
Peshawar
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Peshawar provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
Director (Enforcement) PTA Zonal Office, Plot No. 11, Sector A-3, Phase-V, Hayatabad, Peshawar.

Chairman's Message
At the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), we are committed to building a digitally inclusive, secure, and forward-looking Pakistan. Our mission is to ensure that every citizen regardless of geography or background, has access to reliable, affordable, and high-quality telecommunications and digital services.
In today’s fast evolving world, digital connectivity is no longer a luxury, it is a fundamental enabler for education, healthcare, business, and social inclusion. On this transformative journey, PTA stands as both a catalyst and a guardian of progress, shaping regulatory and licensing landscape guided by technological advancement that not only support innovation but also protect the rights and interests of users.
In line with this commitment, we take pride in remarkable strides made by Pakistan’s telecom sector including record growth in telecom subscribers, substantial expansion of  broadband coverage and the local manufacturing of millions of mobile devices. PTA has also laid the foundation for adoption of future technologies such as 5G, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and advanced Wi-Fi standards, ensuring that Pakistan remains at the forefront of digital transformation. These achievements are not merely milestones for the industry but represent steps toward creating a technologically advanced Pakistan and strengthening the national economy.
Yet, our work is far from done. We are steadfast in our resolve to bridge the digital divide, enhance cybersecurity, encourage public private collaboration, and ensure that Pakistan is ready to embrace the future technological advancements. As we move forward, transparency, consumer protection, and equitable growth will remain at the heart of all our initiatives.
On behalf of PTA, I extend my sincere gratitude to the telecom industry, partners, and the people of Pakistan for their trust and support. Together, we will continue to shape a resilient digital future, one that ensures connectivity, opportunity, safety, and prosperity for the people of Pakistan.

## UNICEF
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/unicef-660310886-2025-02-18

UNICEF
UNICEF
×
Print
UNICEF
Collaboration with UNICEF Pakistan
PTA signed MoU with United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) on March 28th, 2023. Under this MoU, PTA became part of UNICEF global “Disrupting Harm Programme” on COP and Pakistan has become 12th country to be conducting this Knowledge Attitude Practice (KAP) survey. This survey will help in developing COP strategies, policies and targeted awareness campaigns. Furthermore, designed awareness static COP posters and disseminated through SM guiding users about safe and responsible use of internet & parents to play their role in preventing their children against online risks/hazards. The campaign reached 24M views in just 2 weeks PTA allocated the emergency number 1121 to provincial organizations dealing with Child Protection.
Train the Trainer Program with UNICEF
Parents having a key role in safeguarding children from online risks, however, usually parents demonstrate lack of awareness w.r.t online dangers being exposed to children hence not adopting related measures. PTA while realizing the fact has designed “Train the Trainer” program in collaboration with UNICEF Pakistan as only digitally literate parents & teachers can better guide/support their children in developing essential skills in handling online risks/dangers. This multiplier effect will have a significant impact on creating a safer online environment for children and promoting responsible internet usage by children. Master Trainers, after being trained will be required to train more trainers so as to ensure maximum reach. Pilot trainings has been successfully commenced in the cities of Islamabad, Lahore and D.I Khan. Following successful pilot trainings, a 10-day training programme for master trainers was organized in Islamabad from August 1-10, 2024. The training focused on the use of manuals exclusively developed for adolescents and caregivers. These master trainers will subsequently train 210 facilitators, who will then extend this vital training to children, parents, and teachers at the community and school levels. The ToT programme marked a significant step towards making every child and parent digitally literate so that children can thrive in a safer digital environment.
Train the Trainer Program with UNICEF – For Partners
PTA launched a four-day “Training of Trainers” (ToT) program for officials from PTA, UNICEF, Telenor Pakistan, the National Commission on the Rights of Child (NCRC), and the NCERT. The program aimed to enhance awareness of the online risks children encounter and equip officials with strategies to help parents manage their children’s digital activities safely. It is part of a broader 10-day training initiative for 15 master trainers, who will subsequently train 210 facilitators to educate students, parents, and teachers about digital literacy and online safety. Key topics covered in the training included online safety, threats from the Dark Web, and responsible internet usage. Experts from TikTok and Tencent provided valuable insights into safety tools and practices available on their platforms.
During the training, Dr. Khawar Siddique Khokhar, Member Compliance & Enforcement PTA, highlighted the importance of collaborative efforts to safeguard children in the digital realm. He reaffirmed the PTA’s commitment to equipping parents and educators with the necessary resources to ensure children’s online safety and promote responsible internet use. Certificates were awarded to participants by representatives from PTA, UNICEF, and Telenor.
Train the Trainer Program with UNICEF – For PTA Employees
Islamabad (November 7, 2024): Demonstrating its commitment to employee welfare and family support, PTA, in collaboration with UNICEF Pakistan, Telenor, and social media tech companies, carried out a three-day specialized workshop on "Child Online Protection”. The comprehensive training offered insights from prominent leaders at global organizations, including UNICEF Pakistan, ECI, Microsoft, Goog

## Protect Yourself from Scams
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/protect-yourself-from-scams-426281729-2023-05-30

Protect Yourself from Scams
Protect Yourself from Scams
×
Print
Protect Yourself from Scams
a. Scams target everyone
Scammers target people of all backgrounds, ages and income levels across Pakistan.
Scammers create believable stories that may convince you to give them more money or personal details.
b. Protect yourself
Do not open suspicious texts, or click on links or attachments in SMS – ignore and report.
Beware of any requests for your details or money. Never send money or give ATM or PIN details, online account details or copies of personal documents to anyone you don’t know or trust.
You should warn your friends and family about scams.
If you are not sure that you're being scammed, stop sending money. Scammers will keep asking for more money until you stop.
If you have sent money or shared your banking details with a scammer, contact your bank & police immediately. They may be able to stop a transaction, or close your account if the scammer has your account details.
c. Report scams to the authorities
First, report the scam number to your service provider (Jazz, Zong, Telenor, Ufone & PTCL) for blocking of suspected number.
If no response is received from service provider, you can also report the number to PTA for blocking by dialing 0800-55055 or visit https://complaint.pta.gov.pk/RegisterComplaint
PTA will block such number and mobile device IMEI. Repeat offences from the same person (using a different number) will result in blacklisting of such CNICs for issuance of new SIMs/connection
If a financial/banking fraud has occurred, contact State Bank of Pakistan: cpd.helpdesk@sbp.org.pk
For further investigation, contact FIA helpline: 051 9106384

## Collaboration with META
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/collaboration-with-meta-673796713-2025-02-18

Collaboration with META
Collaboration with META
×
Print
Collaboration with META
Chai Chats 2022: PTA in collaboration with META has launched educational series campaigns with the name “Chai Chat” to create awareness among young Pakistani SM users on digital literacy and responsible use of SM. Chai Chats Facebook page: https://web.facebook.com/chaichatspk
Anti-Scams Campaign 2023:  An Anti-Scams Campaign was carried out in Urdu and English for Safer Internet Day (February 7, 2023), to generate impact amongst online buyers and sellers in Pakistan. The campaign contained a series of animated assets, aimed to build knowledge of users, businesses and communities on factors to consider before engaging in E-commerce on Meta Platforms. The campaign went successful as it reached over 37 million users.
Children’s Day Campaign 2023: META joined hands with PTA to release a series of impactful videos targeting children, emphasizing crucial online safety measures. These collaborative videos were designed to educate and empower children to navigate the digital world securely. Following 5x videos regarding safe use of internet were developed and disseminated on Children's Day 2023.
Privacy Check Up: https://fb.watch/otvgCyqQAd/?mibextid=Nif5oz
Locked Profile: https://fb.watch/otvhS_ukD7/?mibextid=Nif5oz
Parental Supervision: https://fb.watch/owAIGtHkU1/?mibextid=Nif5oz
Managing False Information: https://fb.watch/owAJY-OtLp/?mibextid=Nif5oz
Hidden Words: https://fb.watch/owALy3Wi9k/?mibextid=Nif5oz
Anti-Scams Campaign 2024: Recently, PTA & Meta has launched exclusive campaign in 2024, which addressed the following 9 common scam types through a series of static assets and short videos:
Investment Scam
Job Scam
Ecommerce Scam
Messaging
Impersonation Scam
Finance Scam
Loan Scam
Lottery Scam
Celeb-bait Scam
TakeItDown Portal 2024: Based on continuous engagement with Meta regarding launching of Urdu version of the TakeItDown portal, so as to facilitate maximum public, Meta recently launched the same in collaboration of National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) on 3rd July 2024. TakeItDown is a vital tool that can be effectively utilized in combating online child exploitation, a significant step towards a safer internet environment for children and youth.  Experts from Meta along with NCMEC conducted a workshop focusing on promoting internet safety for children and youth, addressing challenges like cyberbullying, privacy breaches etc and usage of TakeItDown portal.

## Collaboration with Telenor
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/collaboration-with-telenor-505529211-2025-02-18

Collaboration with Telenor
Collaboration with Telenor
×
Print
Collaboration with Telenor
PTA is working closely with Telenor and UNICEF to advance Child Online Protection. Along Telenor, UNICEF & NCRC, PTA has collectively launched the Parental Guidebook, "Safeguarding Your Child in the Digital Age." This initiative reflects a shared commitment to equipping parents with the tools and knowledge they need to protect their children in the evolving digital landscape.

## About
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/about-1698007896-2025-02-18

About
About
×
Print
About
Chairman’s Message
It is my pleasure to introduce PTA's dedicated webpage for Child Online Protection. With evolving digital landscape, children now have unprecedented access to information, entertainment, and social connections. While this brings immense opportunities, it also poses challenges demanding vigilance and proactive measures to ensure their safety and well-being in the online world.
This dedicated resource offers essential means to empower children, parents, and caregivers with the knowledge and tools needed to navigate the digital space safely while supporting their educational needs.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) recognizes that Child Online Protection is a global concern requiring national and international collaboration. Although we have made progress, the mission is to establish a safe and secure online environment for children continues.
Parents and caregivers play a crucial role in this journey. By dedicating time, modeling responsible online behavior, and fostering open communication, we can build trust and awareness to effectively support our children in navigating the digital realm.
PTA is committed to providing accessible information and resources to empower all stakeholders, ensuring a safer and more inclusive internet experience for our young users.
Together, through combined efforts and collaboration, we can build a secure digital future for our children.
Video Highlighting PTA’s COP Initiatives and Achievements

## Multan
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/multan-915225562-2023-05-30

Multan
Multan
×
Print
Multan
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Multan provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
Director (Enforcement) PTA Zonal Office, House No.61-A, Main Street Sabzazar, Bosan Road Multan.
For Complaints:

Fax

Address

## Commercial Affairs
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/commercial-affairs-791203798-2023-05-30

Commercial Affairs
Commercial Affairs
×
Print
Commercial Affairs
Functions:
The Commercial Affairs Directorate is mainly responsible for ensuring fair competition in the market. CA division also entrusted to regulate the tariffs of various telecommunication services, keeping in view the consumers' interest and the profitability of telecom operators. It determines operators with significant market power and takes appropriate measures to prohibit dominant operators from anti-competitive practices. CA division also ensures any-to-any connectivity among telecom operators through seamless interconnection with emphasis on establishing interconnection charges that are cost-based, transparent and non-discriminatory. Commercial Affairs division regulates Approved Settlement Rates and coordinates with the Ministry of Information Technology in framing appropriate Rules & Regulations.

## Parental Guidebook Launch Event
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/parental-guidebook-launch-event-1456475945-2025-02-18

Parental Guidebook Launch Event
Parental Guidebook Launch Event
×
Print
Parental Guidebook Launch Event
Event - “Parental Guide: Safeguarding your Child in the Digital Age-Guide for Caregivers & Policy Brief on Child Online Protection” – 20th Feb 2024
COP Committee in collaboration with UNICEF and Telenor organized an event showcasing the work done in the field of Child Online Protection. The event was attended by esteemed guests including the Caretaker Minister for IT & Telecom, Dr. Umar Saif, and representatives from MoIT&T, PTA, Telenor, NCRC, and UNICEF Pakistan, highlighted the critical need to safeguard children online. The event included Panel Discussion on the topic of “Safely Navigating the Digital Age” connected with quizzed based interactive activity through mentimeter for student and caregivers to judge their level of understanding about online safety issues and related measurers.
Launch of Parental Guidebook "Safeguarding your Child in the Digital Age" in collaboration with the National Commission on the Rights of Child (NCRC), UNICEF & Telenor Pakistan. The guide aims to educate parents & caregivers ensuring a secure online environment for children. The guidebook was presented by Chairman PTA to Chief Guest.
The guidebook was also presented by Chairman PTA to Doreen Bogdan-Martin an American diplomat and Engineer, current Secretary-General of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) during Mobile World Congress 2024 in Barcelona.

## Local Loop
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/local-loop-814443771-2023-05-30

Local Loop
Local Loop
×
Print
Local Loop
Public Notice
Pakistan Telecommunication Authority is accepting applications for the grant of Fixed Local Loop (FLL) Licenses for all Telecom Regions in Pakistan, Azad Jammu & Kashmir (AJ&K) and Gilgit-Baltistan (GB).
A Fixed Local Loop (FLL) License authorizes the Licensee to provide the Licensed Services and to establish, maintain and operate a Telecommunication System in the Licensed Region, subject to the terms and conditions of the license.
Apply Online for License (OASIS)
Information Memorandum
FAQs - Local Loop
Application Processing
Document Required for Creating Organization Profile in OASIS
Information to be provided by Applicant
In case Applicants are interested to obtain LL license in more than one region, separate applications shall be filed for each region along with necessary documents on “Online Application Submission Information System (OASIS)”. The total number of regions is 14.
As part of the Application, an Applicant must provide the following:
Letter of Application
Checklist
Fees in the following amounts, payable in Pak Rupees:
Application fee of US $ 500 (or equivalent Forex value in PKR) per Region applied for,
Initial fee – LL License of US $ 10,000/- (or equivalent Forex value in PKR) per Region applied for,
Certificate of Incorporation of the Applicant and its Memorandum and Articles of Association;
Names of the Directors of the Applicant, and relation of each Director to any other Operator licensed by the Authority or any other Applicant for a License;
Shareholders of the Applicant, including details of each shareholder’s equity ownership;
Names of each Affiliate of a shareholder of the Applicant, where the Affiliate is an Operator or an applicant for a License, and description of the relation to the Applicant;
Copies of National Identity Card (for Pakistani nationals) / Passport (foreign nationals) and other antecedents of the Directors and authorized representative of the company.
Provide an undertaking for the following:
That the Company or its Directors have never been declared insolvent by a court of law
That the Directors of the company have never been convicted by a court of law for major offences or unethical/immoral turpitude ( other than minor offences)
That neither the applicant Company nor its group/consortium members are defaulter (s) with reference to other PTA licences/transactions.
Applicant’s National Income tax number;
Certificate on original letterhead from the Group/Joint venture/Consortium members that they are the participants for LL in Pakistan through the applicant company.
Certificate of good standing with the fiscal administration;
Resolution of the Board of Directors of the Applicant authorizing the individual who submits and signs the Application.
Special Power of Attorney by the Applicant authorizing the individual who submits and signs the Application.
A brief description of the following:
Telecommunication experience of the Applicant, its key management personnel and its shareholders.
Business plan for the initial five years of operations, indicating areas to be served, services to be offered, projected revenues, operating expenses and capital requirements.
Committed financial resources including a list of all sources and amounts of equity and debt financing required to finance the business plan in the first 5 years of operation. Capital must show at    least a 20%      equity component.
Technical plan, including proposed network map and architecture.
Affidavit of the person granted the power of attorney by the Applicant.
The Applicant shall submit the application on “Online Application Submission Information System (OASIS).”
Upon receipt, the Authority will provide an acknowledgement of the received Application via “Online Application Submission Information System (OASIS).”
Eligibility Criteria
The following are the eligibility requirements for a License:
The applicant shall be an incorporated or registered company in Pakistan u

## Biometric Verification
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/biometric-verification-771039280-2023-05-30

Biometric Verification
Biometric Verification
×
Print
Biometric Verification
Say “No” to Illegal SIMs!
1.     Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) in collaboration with Cellular Mobile Operators (CMOs) has introduced Multi Random Finger Biometric Verification System (MBVS) to carry out following transactions after online verification from NADRA:
Buy/Activate a new SIM
Get a Duplicate SIM
Change of Ownership of a SIM
Mobile Number Portability (MNP)
Re-verification of SIM
Disowning of SIM
The Danger of Illegal SIMs Registered in Your Name
2.     Illegal SIM cards are those that have been obtained using fraudulent or illegal means, such as using false identity documents or stolen personal information. If such a SIM card is registered in your name without your knowledge or consent, it can pose several dangers, including:
Criminal Activity: Criminals can use illegal SIM cards to carry out fraudulent activities such as identity theft, cybercrime, and financial fraud. If the SIM card is registered in your name, you could be falsely implicated in such criminal activity.
Harassment: If the illegal SIM card is used to harass or threaten others, you could be held responsible for such behavior, and you could face legal consequences.
Financial Loss: If the illegal SIM card is used to make fraudulent transactions or purchases, you could be held liable for the financial loss.
Compromised Privacy: The use of an illegal SIM card can also compromise your privacy, as your personal information and contacts can be accessed by the person using the SIM card.
National Security: Illegal SIM cards can also be used by terrorists or other criminal organizations to plan and execute illegal activities, which can pose a threat to national security.
3.     In summary, having an illegal SIM card registered in your name can pose serious dangers, both legal and personal. It's important to ensure that all SIM cards registered in your name are obtained through legal means and that you take certain steps to protect your personal information from identity theft and fraud.
Steps to Ensure Safety
4.     To ensure your safety and avoid registration of illegal SIM against your credentials, please follow these simple steps:
Only Visit an authorized MBVS Enabled Sale Outlet for above Transactions. Authorized sales outlets include Customer Service Centers (CSC), Franchisees & Registered Retailers having a MBVS Device and an authorization (Card/Letter).
Go through the Terms & Conditions for Purchase of SIM Displayed at the Sale Channel. The same is also available at Customer Service Centers (CSC) and Franchisees.
Provide Valid Computerized National Identity Card (CNIC) Number to Sale Agent
Provide Thumb / Finger Impressions on BVS Scanner for Verification from NADRA. A maximum of two successful thumb/finger impressions are required.
Fraudsters also use a technique to get your finger prints on different machines or even on simple paper in the garb of government officials of different support schemes. Therefore, it should be ensured that finger prints are applied on machines only to trusted parties and no finger prints are given in paper at all.
In Case of Successful Verification, SIM Shall be Activated & Handed-over to You
In Case of Un-Successful Verification, Sale Agent Shall Inform the Reason and Provide Further Guidance
Make Sure to Collect Your SIM after Biometric Verification. In Case the Sale Agent does not Handover the SIM, please lodge your complaint with following Information to PTA:
CNIC Number
Date of Visit
Company Whose Sale Channel was Visited
Name & Address of Sale Channel
Old Age Individuals and Persons with Amputation, whose biometric verification is not possible, can get SIMs from Customer Service Centers (CSCs) and Selected Franchisees after Verification through Administrative Means
No Prize/Gift Scheme Requires Biometric Verification. Lately, certain Gangs have been Caught seeking Thumb/Finger impressions from general public in the garb of membersh

Child Online Protection (COP) was made part of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between GSMA and PTA during the Mobile World Congress 2024 in Barcelona with the aim to enhance collaboration for ensuring safer internet for children.
Through collaborative efforts, GSMA will share knowledge, build capacity, and advocate jointly for the development of best practices, ensuring a safer digital environment for children.

## Collaboration with ITU
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/collaboration-with-itu-1473730603-2025-02-18

Collaboration with ITU
Collaboration with ITU
×
Print
Collaboration with ITU
Translation of ITU Mascot Sango “Online Safety with Sango”:
International Telecommunication Union (ITU) created mascot “Online Safety with Sango”, for Sangophone, ITU’s child online protection so as to empower children to perform activities freely in the digital sphere. Sango guides children through five different lessons in a fun and friendly way. The metaphor was designed to help children understand the importance of keeping themselves and their personal data protected and safe. PTA’ COP committee translated the guide booklet in Urdu language to provide children with lessons in a fun and friendly way.
ITU Council Working Group CWG on Child Online Protection (Upcoming):
ITU Council established the Council Working Group on Child Online Protection (WG-CP) with the following terms of reference:
To exchange views and promote and work on the subject matter.
To report to the Council annually on the activities of the working group on child online protection (WG-CP).
Recognizing PTA’s efforts to promote a safer Internet for children, ITU included PTA in its Council Working Group on Child Online Protection (CWG-COP). PTA participated in the 21st CWG-COP meeting held from September 30 to October 1, 2024, in Geneva, Switzerland, where it showcased successes achieved through collaborations with UNICEF, TikTok, GSMA, Meta, and others. The Chair praised PTA’s collaborative approach with the private sector as a model for global adoption and requested PTA to share its Urdu-translated COP resources with ITU to enhance global outreach. ITU also offered support for wider dissemination of these resources. A detailed report on PTA’s COP initiatives can be accessed at https://www.itu.int/md/S24-CLCWGCOP21-INF/en
PTA participation in 22nd meeting of International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council Working Group on Child Online Protection (CWG-COP)
PTA's participated in the 22nd ITU Council Working Group on Child Online Protection (CWG-COP) meeting on 12-13 Feb 2025. ITU acknowledged PTA's initiatives by featuring them on their official website (https://www.itu.int/md/S25-CLCWGCOP22-  INF/en). Head of COP Committee presented comprehensive efforts and initiatives for 2024, focusing on following key areas:
•    Strategic collaborations with international and national organizations
•    Implementation of digital literacy programs for students, parents, and caregivers
•    Development of Urdu-language content and resources
The Chair commended PTA's efforts, particularly highlighting collaborative approach to addressing children's online risks, describing it as a role model for other countries to follow.

## Abbottabad
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/abbottabad-7358821-2023-05-30

Abbottabad
Abbottabad
×
Print
Abbottabad
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Abbottabad provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
PTA Zonal Office Abbottabad, House No. 267/A, Main Mansehra Road, Supply Bazar, Abbottabad

## STACA Division
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/staca-division-204164715-2025-02-26

STACA Division
STACA Division
×
Print
STACA Division
Functions:
The STACA Division of PTA is responsible for overseeing standards, testing, and accreditation within the telecom sector. It plays a key role in formulating technical regulations, ensuring compliance with industry standards, and evaluating telecom equipment for approval and certification. The division also collaborates with stakeholders to enhance regulatory policies, promote technological advancements, and facilitate a secure and standardized telecom environment in Pakistan.

## Quetta
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/quetta-1096320039-2023-05-30

Quetta
Quetta
×
Print
Quetta
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Quetta provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
Director (Enforcement) PTA Zonal Office, Near FIA Building, Samungli Road Quetta.

## National | NT CERT
- **Source URL**: https://ntcert.pta.gov.pk/national.html

National | NT CERT
National Collaboration
Home
National Collaboration
National Collaboration
At the forefront of national cyber security, Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) is committed to fostering strong collaborative partnerships. As part of this initiative, PTA signed Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with two key national organizations to enhance cyber resilience and security:
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team of Pakistan (National CERT)
Securities & Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP)
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team of Pakistan (National CERT)
A significant step towards enhancing cyber security in Pakistan was taken when a delegation from National CERT of Pakistan visited PTA headquarters in Islamabad. This visit marked the beginning of a robust collaboration aimed at strengthening cyber secure digital initiatives in the country.
National CERT team commended PTA’s efforts in safeguarding critical telecom data and infrastructure, which has significantly enhanced public trust in the nation’s telecommunication and internet services.
Both organizations pledged to work together towards the shared goal of achieving a cyber secure digital Pakistan. A dedicated interface has been established to facilitate technical and operational cooperation.
The meeting concluded with a mutual commitment to closely collaborate in addressing the evolving cyber threats at the national level, ensuring a secure digital environment for Pakistan.
Click here or more details
Securities & Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP)
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) and the Securities & Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) have formalized their collaboration by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). This strategic partnership aims to address issues within their respective regulatory domains, ensuring a more secure and regulated digital environment in Pakistan.Key initiatives agreed upon include:
PTA and SECP will establish a joint mechanism to monitor and report on illegal lending apps, enhancing regulatory oversight and consumer protection.
SECP informed PTA of its efforts in building a comprehensive cybersecurity framework, aiming to fortify the digital financial sector against cyber threats
Both organizations agreed to launch a joint awareness campaign to educate the public about the risks associated with illegal digital lending apps in Pakistan. This initiative will promote safer digital financial practices and protect consumers from potential fraud.
Click here or more details

## Cellular Mobile
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/cellular-mobile-1185498158-2023-05-30

Cellular Mobile
Cellular Mobile
×
Print
Cellular Mobile
Cellular mobile licensing process is initiated in accordance with Policy Directives by GoP, once such a directive is issued, Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) initiates the licensing process. This process includes the preparation of an Information Memorandum, stakeholders consultation, spectrum auction, and subsequent award of licenses. For more details please visit Spectrum Auctions.
Currently, there are four cellular mobile operators in Pakistan: Pakistan Mobile Communication Limited (Jazz), CMPak Limited (Zong), Telenor Pakistan and PTML (Ufone). These operators provide cellular mobile and broadband services across Pakistan.
In Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJ&K) and Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), five cellular mobile operators are providing cellular mobile and broadband services. These operators are Special Communication Organization (SCO), Telenor Pakistan, CMPak Ltd (Zong), Pakistan Mobile Communication Limited (Jazz) and PTML (Ufone).

## IR&GA
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/government-and-external-affairs-625549262-2023-05-30

IR&GA
IR&GA
×
Print
IR&GA
Functions:
The International Relations & Government Affairs Division of PTA is responsible for managing engagements with international regulatory bodies, governments, and stakeholders to ensure alignment of Pakistan’s telecom policies with global standards. The division plays a key role in fostering diplomatic ties, representing PTA in global forums, and ensuring compliance with international telecom regulations. It liaises with global telecom regulatory bodies such as ITU and GSMA, participates in international conferences, and coordinates with government ministries, policymakers, and diplomatic missions on telecom policies and regulations. Additionally, this Division also organize and oversee PR activities and ensure effective communication with stakeholders, media and the public.

## Sukkur
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/sukkur-1110312189-2023-05-30

Sukkur
Sukkur
×
Print
Sukkur
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Sukkur provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
H. No. 146, Sindhi Muslim Cooperative Housing Society, Airport Road, Sukkur.

Email

Cyber Vigilance
Cyber Vigilance
×
Print
Cyber Vigilance
Functions:
Cyber Vigilance Division is providing assistance & feedback on policy formulation. Cyber Security is responsible to carry out internal & external security audit of applications and infrastructure. The directorate is also issuing advisories and guidelines to deal with cyber threats and to ensure implementation of security controls in systems to avoid any unforeseen circumstances

## History
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/history-1584422891-2023-05-30

History
History
×
Print
History
The Pakistan Telecommunication Ordinance 1994, established the primary regulatory framework for the telecommunication industry including the establishment of an authority. Thereafter, Telecommunication (Re-Organization) Act no XVII was promulgated in 1996 that aimed to reorganize the telecom sector of Pakistan. Under Telecom Reorganization Act 1996, Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) was established to regulate the establishment, operation and maintenance of telecommunication systems, and the provision of telecom services.
PTA has its headquarters at Islamabad and zonal offices located at Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Quetta, Rawalpindi, Muzaffarabad, Gilgit Baltistan, Abbottabad, Faisalabad, Gwadar, Multan and Sukkur.

## Collaboration with Council of Islamic Ideology
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/collaboration-with-council-of-islamic-ideology-1729590890-2025-02-18

Collaboration with Council of Islamic Ideology
Collaboration with Council of Islamic Ideology
×
Print
Collaboration with Council of Islamic Ideology
PTA in collaboration with Council of Islamic Ideology has invited renowned Ulama-e-Karam from all over the Pakistan in a conference held on October 10, 2023. PTA took a significant step toward fostering safe and responsible internet usage by organizing a meeting with prominent religious scholars at PTA Headquarters, Islamabad. The event, marked a collaborative effort between the PTA and religious leaders to address the challenges of social media and the internet while promoting a digital environment that aligns with cultural and religious values.
The meeting was attended by Islamic scholars from various schools of thought including Dr. Qibla Ayaz, Chairman Council of Islamic Ideology (CII); Moulana Abdul Khabeer Azad, Chairman Ruet-e-Hilal Committee and Maulana Tariq Jameel among others. Senior PTA officers were also present at this occasion. The event commenced with a welcome note from Director-General, Web Analysis Division (WAD) PTA, who provided an overview of PTA's initiatives.
Chairman PTA, Maj General (R) Hafeez Ur Rehman addressed the audience and highlighted the pivotal role of religious scholars in guiding the masses toward ethical and responsible internet usage. He emphasized the potential for even greater impact if the scholars lend their support to PTA through their own platforms.
An open-floor discussion and recommendation session provided a platform for active engagement and dialogue. Key highlights of the meeting included a strong emphasis to educate the youth about responsible social media and internet usage especially the critical role of parents in educating their children. The Quran & teachings of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) were highlighted as a guiding light in this endeavor.
Recognizing the gravity of online threats such as anti-state, blasphemous and hate speech online, it was emphasized that addressing them is the collective responsibility of the State, judiciary, PTA, PEMRA, FIA and the individuals.
The scholars expressed their appreciation for PTA's commitment and efforts in promoting safe and responsible internet usage and reassured their full cooperation and support to the regulator. This meeting marks the beginning of a series, towards collaborative efforts with respected Ulema to combat harmful and unlawful online content.

## Finance Division
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/finance-division-920174455-2025-01-31

Finance Division
Finance Division
×
Print
Finance Division
Functions:
Finance Division of PTA is envisaged for formulating and implementing the core financial functions of the organization. This Divisions consists of three Directorates i.e Finance, Payroll & Cash and Budget & Account. Finance Directorate is mainly responsible for receivable management with aim to ensure timely invoicing and collection of receivables. Finance Directorate actively engages with licensees to address any related matters. Payroll & Cash directorate deals with payroll, tax related matters and payable to vendor. Budget & Account directorate look after preparation of budget as required under section 12 of the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) Act, 1996 and monitoring of budget. Budget & Accounts directorate also prepares Financial statements of PTA and also manages its audit by commercial auditors.

## Web Analysis
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/web-analysis-451424982-2023-05-30

Web Analysis
Web Analysis
×
Print
Web Analysis
Functions:
Web Analysis Division of PTA is responsible to analyse, channalise and process the URLs for blocking having Blasphemous, Anti-state, Hate Speech, Pornographic, etc. content reported by different Government Departments, General Public etc. Blocking of the unlawful content is carried out either by approaching the concerned online platform(s) or the Cyber Vigilance Division of PTA, as the case may be. The Division also maintains an online portal for recording complaints received from different Government departments.

## Higher Education Commission (HEC)
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/higher-education-commission-hec-345215216-2025-02-18

Higher Education Commission (HEC)
Higher Education Commission (HEC)
×
Print
Higher Education Commission (HEC)
MoU Signing with Higher Education Commission (HEC)
Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) and the Higher Education Commission (HEC) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on December 9, 2024. This collaboration aims to foster technological innovation and address dynamic policy and regulatory challenges.
The collaborative model between PTA and HEC is expected to drive improvements in areas such as curriculum development, the creation of specialized training programs, regulatory innovation workshops, and aligning research with real-world problems by incorporating inputs from experts in the telecom/ICT industry.
Ongoing Collaborations with Higher Education Commission (HEC)
PTA in collaboration with HEC is raising awareness in educational institutions of Pakistan regarding safe and responsible use of internet & Social Media.
HEC Seminars
Sensitized VCs of over 165 Universities about the wide circulation of blasphemous content and emphasized on playing active role in raising awareness among youngsters for responsible and legitimate use of internet.
Participated as a speaker in seminar held on October 4, 2023 on “Awareness Regarding Prevention of Blasphemous Material/Activities on Social Media”.
Participated as a speaker in seminars held at following universities & colleges regarding raising awareness about spreading blasphemous content & responsible use of social media:
Wafaqi Mohtasib & COMSATS University - November 20, 2023.
NUTECH University - January 3, 2024.
University of Karachi - February 13, 2024.

SAMENA LEAD Award 2023
SAMENA council (South Asia Middle East North Africa Telecommunications) a tri-regional association spanning 25+ countries representing the interests of more than 85 telecom operators and service providers, announced international LEAD award for PTA under “Enabling Child & Youth Safety Online”.

## Recognise scams
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/recognise-scams-893680852-2023-05-30

Recognise scams
Recognise scams
×
Print
Recognise scams
Scammers will go to great lengths to convince you that a fortune awaits if you follow their instructions.
You may be introduced to a second or even third scammer – posing as a banker, TV channel representative or government official – to 'help facilitate the legal and financial aspects of the transaction’.
Some of the common scams include:
a)         Attempts to gain your personal information
Scammers use all kinds of approaches to steal personal details. Once obtained, they can use the stolen identity to commit fraudulent activities.
b)         Impersonating Banks/Organizations
Scammers impersonate genuine organizations such as banks/Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP)/ Ehsas Programme etc. A common fraud technique is that your “ATM has been blocked” and that you should call a number (listed in the message) to get your ATM unblocked.
Another technique used by scammers is to pretend to be representatives of PTA and ask for money in guise of registration of mobile device.
c)         Threats & extortion
Scammers try to steal identity or money – including threatening the life of the person they are calling. Popular technique used by scammers impersonating Pakistan Army.
d)         Cash Transfer/”Sending a code”
Scammers invent convincing and seemingly legitimate reasons to lull the receiver of message or caller into a false sense of security. For example: a popular technique is to send the receiver a message about transferring money into their Easy Paisa or other e-payment account by mistake and to send a certain “code” or “message” back to them.
e)         Prize/Lottery Scams
Scammers trick you into giving money or your personal information in order to receive a prize from a lottery or competition that you may have never entered. Such scammers usually impersonate popular TV game show programmes.

## Regulatory Compliance & Operations (RC&O) Division
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/regulatory-compliance-&-operations-rc&o-division-1188711416-2025-02-26

Regulatory Compliance & Operations (RC&O) Division
Regulatory Compliance & Operations (RC&O) Division
×
Print
Regulatory Compliance & Operations (RC&O) Division
Functions:
Regulatory Compliance and Operations (RC&O) Division has been established with a view to strengthen compliance related matters with focus on off-field actions to enforce provisions of PTA’s Act, Regulations, SOPs and directions of Authority received from time to time. RC&O Division communicates/coordinates with Armed Forces/Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) on National Security matters and other Government Agencies on need basis. It deals with issues pertaining to verification of mobile subscribers’ antecedents through multifarious interventions.

## Lahore
- **Source URL**: https://www.pta.gov.pk/category/lahore-73871969-2023-05-30

Lahore
Lahore
×
Print
Lahore
Services:
PTA Zonal Office, Lahore provides following services
Promote rapid modernization of telecommunication systems and telecommunication services.
Promote and protect the interests of users of telecommunication services.
Carry out inspections of PTA licensees.
Prompt disposal of complaints against telecom operators.
Provide assistance to the public for the issuance of licenses by the Headquarters
Provide assistance to the general public for usage/installation of PTA approved GSM signal boosters.
Conduct regular and systematic inspections of PTA licensees to ensure strict adherence to licensing conditions and regulatory frameworks.
Action against illegal telecom operators and activation of SIMs without user consent.
Provide assistance to the public regarding DIRBS & IMEI Blocking of stolen/snatched mobile devices.
Contact:
PTA Zonal Office – Adjacent Cantt Telephone Exchange
165-Abid Majeed Road, Lahore (042)
